memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But when they told him everything Joseph had said to them, and when he saw the carts Joseph had sent to carry him back, the spirit of their father Jacob revived. And Israel said, 'I'm convinced! My son Joseph is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.'" — Gen 45:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What finally convinced Jacob? Two things: the words Joseph had said, and the carts he had sent.

The message alone was not enough — he had heard it and gone numb. But then he saw the evidence. Real carts, standing in his yard, sent by someone with the power to send them. Word and evidence together, and something inside the old man came back to life. "The spirit of their father Jacob revived."

Then something beautiful happens in the text. He is called Jacob while he is grieving, and Israel — his covenant name, the name God gave him — the moment faith returns. Faith restores a man to who God says he is.

Notice too that God gives us both word and evidence. We have the message of the gospel, and we have the Spirit given to us as a deposit guaranteeing what is to come (Eph 1:13-14). Not carts in the yard, but something better — God Himself living in us as the pledge of everything He has promised.

Jacob's last chapter began at eighty-something years old with a journey he never expected to make. Whatever you thought was finished for you, God may not have finished with it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God used to revive your spirit in a low season?
2. Are you living out of your grief, or out of who God says you are?
3. What has God promised that you can hold onto today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, revive my spirit where it has grown weary. Thank You for Your Word and for Your Spirit within me as the guarantee of everything You have promised. Let me live as who You say I am. Amen.
